questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Indonesia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Indonesia article.

questions.proof: The capital of Indonesia is Jakarta, on the island of Java, but there are plans to change it to Nusantara.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Indonesia about 1,916,907 square kilometres; Uzbekistan about 448,978 square kilometres; Fiji about 18,274 square kilometres; Vanuatu about 12,190 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Indonesia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Indonesia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Indonesia article.

questions.proof: Other nearby countries are Papua New Guinea, Malaysia, and East Timor which share land borders with Indonesia.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Jakarta?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Indonesia is Jakarta.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Indonesia?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Indonesia is the rupiah.
